resources.string: Show the handle while an app is in the foreground
Off: new instances open fullscreen. On: they float over the current screen
Drag the handle, release to snap to the nearest edge
Grant usage access (to detect the foreground app)
This device has no native window mode; falling back to AOSP freeform, which looks different.
Window mode needs freeform windows. Enable “Force activities to be resizable” or “Enable freeform windows” in Developer options.
Swipe the edge handle, or tap “New window” in Quick Settings, to open another instance of the app you are in.
The handle floats above whichever app you are using. Without this permission it cannot be drawn at all.
In system settings, find Morg and allow “Display over other apps”.
Morg reads which app is in the foreground so the handle can stay hidden on the home screen and in Recents. The data never leaves your device.
Open the usage access list and turn Morg on.
Turn the switch on in Developer options, then come back and tap “Try a window”. Seeing one window pop up and closing it is the confirmation.
While the handle runs, a persistent notification carries a “Stop” button. Without it, a handle covering the screen would be hard to turn off.
Declining only hides that notification; the handle still works.
Checking whether this window is really a small window…
A small window opened correctly. Closing it finishes the check.
This opened fullscreen, so the small window is not working yet. Turn on “Enable freeform windows” in Developer options.
No window capability detected yet. Turn on “Enable freeform windows” in Developer options first.
Could not open the check window. Try again in a moment.
Small window still not working — check Developer options
Swipe the handle or tap “New window” in Quick Settings
Morg opens another instance of the app you are already using. Two ways in: the edge handle, or “New window” in the Control Center.
Once on, pull the drawer from the screen edge in any app. The first time you turn it on, Morg walks you through two required permissions.
Fullscreen by default. Turn it on to open new instances in a floating window you can see alongside the original.
Put a “New window” button in the Control Center (swipe down twice → edit → drag it in). It works without the edge handle.
New instances open fullscreen by default. With this on, they open in a floating window while the original stays behind. Window mode needs system support, so confirm it once before turning it on.
“Try a window” opens a small window and closes it again. If it really comes up small, window mode works.
